messages:
alex: quick heads-up: hotfix deploy for payments is blocked. GH Actions runs keep failing on fetching packages from GitHub Packages/npm registry (npm.pkg.github.com) — seeing 502/503 in the logs. Deploy job fails at 'npm install' on our CI runners. Not sure if transient but started ~5m ago. @ops-sre @priya

priya: ack. can you paste the workflow failure logs? any 503s from api.github.com or from npm.pkg.github.com?

alex: here's the snippet:
```
npm ERR! fetch failed https://npm.pkg.github.com/@ourorg/core/-/core-1.2.3.tgz 502 Bad Gateway
npm WARN retry will retry, error on last attempt: Error: 502 Bad Gateway
```
No rate limit headers. Also seeing GH Actions runner errors like "failed to download artifact: unexpected EOF" on some steps.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: third_party_dependency (github-packages) — severity: HIGH. Paging SRE oncall.

ops-sre: I'm on it. I'm seeing increased error rate to github package endpoints from our hosted runners (eu-west and us-west). Checking GH status: https://www.githubstatus.com/ (looks like "Partial Outage" for GitHub Packages). Also checking if GitHub Actions itself reports degradations.

jon: FYI this blocks all hotfix builds; we can't create a new hotfix image via CI which blocks immediate rollback or patch. Current options: 1) wait for GH to recover; 2) build images locally on a runner with cached packages; 3) use mirror registry / proxy (we have an internal npm proxy at https://artifact-cache.redwood.internal) ; 4) manually upload a prebuilt image artifact to ECR/GCR and trigger deployment.

sara: ops-sre, can we flip pipelines to use artifact-cache proxy as fallback? We have a config toggle in the repo: `CI_NPM_REGISTRY` env var. But we need to ensure packages are present in proxy; for @ourorg scoped packages we push from main CI — might be sparse.

ops-sre: I can trigger a cache-populate for the critical package bundle (core, payments, auth). If we can't fetch from GitHub, we can pull from a backup mirror (we keep last 30 builds in internal S3). I will try to re-publish the tarballs to artifact-cache. Give me 10-15m.

priya: note customer impact: feature-x hotfix contains billing fix — customers doing billing changes might experience failed invoice generation if we don't deploy. We should set status page to "degraded" for affected endpoints and notify support with a short blurb.

alex: +1 on status notice. Draft message for support: "We're experiencing issues building hotfixes due to an outage affecting GitHub Packages / Actions. Builds and deployments are delayed. We're working on a workaround and will provide updates every 15 minutes."

deploy-bot: :gear: CI pipeline halted for branch hotfix/payments — blocked by npm install failures.

ops-sre: update — I was able to fetch core-1.2.3 from our internal S3 mirror and re-published to artifact-cache. Trying a manual runner build now using a self-hosted runner in our infra (bypasses GH-hosted runners' network path). If that succeeds we can push images to ECR and trigger deployment via the console.

jon: instructions for manual build (on infra-runner):
```
export CI_NPM_REGISTRY=https://artifact-cache.redwood.internal
git checkout hotfix/payments
yarn install --registry $CI_NPM_REGISTRY
yarn build:docker
docker tag app:latest ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/app:hotfix-1802
aws ecr put-image --repository-name redwood/app --image-tag hotfix-1802 --image-manifest $(docker save app:latest | base64)
```
Note: use `aws ecr` push flow we normally use (we have helper script `scripts/push-ecr.sh`).

sara: ops-sre reports manual runner build succeeded and image pushed to ECR. Starting canary deploy to 10% traffic. Monitoring logs and error rates.

ops-sre: canary looks good so far, no regression. Rolling to 50%.

priya: support notified. Support message: "We've implemented a temporary workaround: we built and pushed a hotfix image using our internal runners and an internal package mirror. Deploy is underway; customers may see intermittent issues for up to 30 minutes."

alex: excellent. Quick followups for post-incident: - add artifact-cache as an automatic fallback in CI (toggle), - document emergency manual build runbook (we had scattered notes), - evaluate self-hosted runners for critical paths.

ops-sre: agreed. Creating follow-up ticket and tagging eng-sre and devex. Also filing an incident report referencing GitHub status incident and our mitigation steps.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated: MAJOR -> MITIGATED (third_party_dependency). Next steps: post-incident review scheduled, collect CI logs and timeline.

jon: one more note — we should re-run full test suite on master once GH services recover to ensure no undetected issues from the mirrored packages.

sara: thanks everyone. I'll stay on watch for another 15m before closing this thread. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks all. :pray:
